_meta.description: Derived golden cases (typedstandards#113 G0 D11). No reference implementation emits these sub-types, vcsRef, or raw-bytes/v1 over a BlobRef, so nothing can be captured. Each case takes one captured case of reference-golden.json as its base, changes only what `change` lists, and states the specification row it follows. Its expected bytes were written by hand from that row, not produced by produce-core or by verify-core's canonicalizer.
derivation: 1. The RFC 8785 canonical string of each base case (withdraws, v01-default) was written by hand: keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit, no whitespace, fields the input leaves undefined omitted. baseCanonical below holds both; their SHA-256 values equal the captured contentHashSha256 and nodeId / envelopeHash of reference-golden.json, which the test asserts.

2. Each derived string is its base string with the change written in by hand at its sorted position: the sub-type URI and the payload fields of the SPEC 8.12.1 row (withdraws' reason and effectiveAt removed); the vcsRef object of the ADR-0016 B table, which sorts last; the raw-bytes/v1 URI and the BlobRef object of legacy-blobref-output as output.

3. jcsWithContentHash is jcsWithoutContentHash with the member contentHash:{sha256:<hex>} inserted after contentCanonicalization, the first key. For legacy-json/v1 the hex is SHA-256 of jcsWithoutContentHash; for raw-bytes/v1 over a BlobRef it is the hex part of output.ref, which is SHA-256 of contentBytesUtf8.
4. contentHashSha256, nodeId and envelopeHash were computed with SHA-256 over those strings. The test recomputes every one with node:crypto alone.
